title: Undo/Redo History Stack using Mutable Refs
concept: Fast History Buffer without Component State Re-renders
problemStatement: Implement `createHistoryBuffer(initialState, maxDepth = 10)` that maintains undo/redo stacks within a mutable ref buffer. Provides `set(state)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, and `canUndo() / canRedo()`.
interviewTrap: Storing undo/redo stacks in React state causes every intermediate history snapshot to re-render the whole editor. Storing history in refs avoids re-renders until an actual restore occurs.

testCases.name: Correctly steps backward with undo()
testCases.testFn: const h = createHistoryBuffer(0); h.set(1); h.set(2); return h.undo();

testCases.name: Correctly steps forward with redo()
testCases.testFn: const h = createHistoryBuffer(0); h.set(1); h.set(2); h.undo(); return h.redo();

testCases.name: Clears future redo stack when new state is pushed
testCases.testFn: const h = createHistoryBuffer(0); h.set(1); h.set(2); h.undo(); h.set(3); return h.canRedo();

details.name: Clears future redo stack when new state is pushed

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: `useRef(initial)` returns a plain JS object `{ current: initial }` that is guaranteed to be the exact same object reference on every render. Mutating `ref.current = value` is completely synchronous and NEVER triggers a component re-render.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Fast History Buffer without Component State Re-renders.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Fast History Buffer without Component State Re-renders maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal

edgeCasesHandled: Storing undo/redo stacks in React state causes every intermediate history snapshot to re-render the whole editor. Storing history in refs avoids re-renders until an actual restore occurs.

specifications: React Fiber Architecture Specification & Runtime Implementation
verifiedRules: Hooks must be called in exact order matching the fiber memoizedState linked list.
